title: Building a Data Quality Framework End-to-End

scenes.title: Building a Data Quality Framework End-to-End
scenes.subtitle: Assembling the pieces into a system
scenes.narration: An end-to-end data quality framework combines validation, observability, contracts, and response into one coherent system.

scenes.heading: Layers of the framework
bullets: Contracts define expectations at the source
Validation gates enforce rules in the pipeline
Lineage powers impact and root-cause analysis
Alerting and SLOs drive response and accountability
scenes.narration: Contracts push expectations to the producer so quality starts upstream. Validation gates enforce concrete rules as data moves through the pipeline. Observability continuously watches health for the unexpected, lineage connects incidents to causes and consumers, and alerting tied to SLOs closes the loop with accountable response.

scenes.heading: End-to-end quality lifecycle
steps: Validate and gate data on ingestion
Monitor the five pillars in production
scenes.narration: The lifecycle begins by agreeing contracts with producers so expectations are explicit. Data is then validated and gated on ingestion to stop known defects early. In production the five pillars are monitored continuously, incidents are traced through lineage to their root cause, and response is measured against SLOs while feeding continuous improvement.

scenes.heading: Wiring the framework in a pipeline
scenes.narration: This orchestration shows the layers working in sequence on each batch. The contract is enforced first, then validation gates the data before it loads. After loading, observability computes metrics across the pillars, and any anomaly opens an incident enriched with lineage and routed as an SLO-driven alert.

scenes.text: A framework is layers working together: contracts, validation, observability, lineage, and SLO-driven response.
scenes.narration: No single technique is enough on its own, but composed together they cover prevention, detection, diagnosis, and response. Build incrementally and let each layer reinforce the others.
